actual.value:
Methodology Guide including research tools, guidelines and analysis frameworks is developed.

title.narrative: 1.1: To develop research instruments for general population surveys
Means of verification: The designed survey material is stored in the UNODC archive. Research instruments are developed for regular surveys on smuggling of migrants

target.value: Designing survey instruments including sampling framework, questionnaires and language translation. The survey focus on the main area of aspiration, preparation and planning of irregular migration journeys using smugglers.
Adapting questionnaires to different local contexts taking sociolinguistic and cultural aspects into consideration
Testing, review and quality assurance of survey instruments
Specialized instrument developed

actual.value:
Quantitative research tools developed for migrant and smuggler respondents.
Surveys designed in partnership with Mixed Migration Centre (MMC)

target.value: The designed survey material is stored in the UNODC archive.

title.narrative: 2.1: To collect data on migrant's aspirations, preparation and planning to contact smugglers
Data collected on migrant’s aspirations, preparation and planning to contact smugglers

target.value: Preparation of procurement of sub-contractor to carry out surveys.
Selection of survey countries.
Comissioning of three general population surveys focussing on the aspirations to migrate, intentions to contacts smugglers and planning efforts of migrants.
Three general population surveys launched collecting information on smuggling of migrants.

actual.value:
Q1-Q4: Regular surveys are being conducted with migrant in North Africa (Libya, Tunisia) and West Africa (Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso) in coordination with MMC.
Q1/Q2: Diplomatic efforts are ongoing to conduct surveys in additional countries in West and North Africa and Europe

target.value: Regular surveys conducted with migrants throughout 2021 and smugglers in North and West Africa.

actual.value: Quantitative data collection carried out on smuggling of migrants in 5 countries, implemented in partnership with Mixed Migration Centre (MMC): 5,240 surveys with people on the move (refugees and migrants) and 500 surveys with migrant smugglers

title.narrative: 2.2: To collect data on specific aspects of migrant smuggling including business models, routes, price development, human costs and law enforcement responses
Qualitative data and information collected on specific aspects of migrant smuggling including business models, routes, price development, human costs and law enforcement responses.

target.value: Preparation of field assesment missions and liaison with national goverments.
Actual field missions and interviews with up to 20 respondents per mission.

Regular surveys conducted with smugglers throughout 2021 in North and West Africa.
In-depth interview with migrants, smugglers & experts conducted in Q2, Q3 and Q4 2021.
Four assessment field missions and qualitative data collection through semi-structured interviews.

actual.value:
Primary and secondary data was collected on specific aspects of migrant smuggling through multiple assessment field missions, in coordination with national Governments, and in partnership with MMC.
Primary qualitative data was collected in Italy, Morocco, Nigeria, Spain, and the Netherlands.
Surveys with migrant smugglers in Burkina Faso Libya, Mali, Niger and Tunisia, Q3 2021.
Qualitative interviews in Libya, Mali, Niger, Tunisia, Burkina Faso, Q4 2021.
Qualitative data collected in Canary Islands Spain in Q4 2021

target.value: Four assessment field missions and qualitative data collection through semi-structured interviews.

title.narrative: 2.3: To analyse and present collected data
Disseminated data and information on smuggling of migrants through the UNODC webpage.

target.value: Quantitative and qualitative analysis of data collected from general population surveys.
Qualitative analysis of information collected from assesment missions and interviews with practitioners and migrants.

Observatory website launched in Q2 2021.
Regular analysis of quantitative and qualitative data conducted.

actual.value:
Observatory online platform launched (in May 2021): www.unodc.org/res/som, which was accessed more than 8,000 times to date.
4 StoryMaps published and downloaded more than 1,900 times to date.
MMC and Observatory published 8 4Mi Snapshots.
2 Observatory research updates published.
Over 36 dissemination events and initiatives to ensure that the Observatory’s findings influence policy.
Observatory contributions to key policy-relevant reports and publications: 4 contributions to other UN publications; and 10 contributions to UN Secretary General, Security Council, Working Group reports and briefs.
The StoryMaps have been used to conduct narrative analysis and data visualisation

target.value: Analysis of primary data and information collected in origin. transit and destination countries.

actual.value: Observatory online platform launched. - StoryMap1 was published. - StoryMap 2 was published. - StoryMaps 3 and 4 in production. - MMC and Observatory published 6 4Mi Snapshots.

title.narrative: 1.3: To explore big data approaches. Memo developed on use of big data techniques to analyze smuggling of migrants
Developed internal learning memo summarizing key points from the workshop and outlining future actions.

target.value: Developed internal learning memo summarizing key points from the workshop and outlining future actions.

actual.value: EGM on illicit financial flows in smuggling of migrants and trafficking in persons took place on 21-22 February 2021, which included the discussed on the role of data collection by financial institutions.

target.value: Enhanced understanding of the use of big data.

actual.value: Expert Group Meeting (EGM) EGM on illicit financial flows associated with smuggling of migrants and trafficking in persons took place on 21-22 February 2021, which included discussion on the role of data collection by financial institutions. A second follow-up EGM on this topic, under other funding, took place on 11-12 October 2022, and a study on this topic will be published by UNODC in 2023.

target.value: Workshop organized with participation of international experts exploring big data usage to understand transnational crime.
Big data collection tested in suitable contexts.
